description: Mastering anything requires a willingness to be the fool. It is equal parts terrifying and exhilarating to try something new. Too much comfort, and we start sleepwalking through life. We lose our sense of wonder. If I confine myself to a handful of roles, I’m shaving down pieces of myself to fit into an ideology. To always be a new student of life means to surprise ourselves and grow a sense of confidence that we really can do anything. We will always be masters and students simultaneously for the rest of our lives. So be intentional with it, and live life as it truly is— a classroom of the human experience.

title: Ballet has been so many things for me. It’s been heaven and an escape. Hell and a prison. Through hours of pouring sweat and soul onto the dance floor, I have found a work ethic and a determination I
description:
Ballet has been so many things for me. It’s been heaven and an escape. Hell and a prison. Through hours of pouring sweat and soul onto the dance floor, I have found a work ethic and a determination I wouldn’t trade for the world. The ability to look resistance square in the eyes and keep going. Yet, I’ve also pushed myself over the edge striving for perfection. 

When you get that first pair of point shoes, they’re stiff. Snug to the bone, they must be broken in through time and dedication. Eventually there is a level of trust, until finally over time they can no longer hold you up and we have to once again find a new shoe that fits.

Art is like this. We’re new students, stumbling and finding our way until we get the hang of something. Eventually, we outgrow our own work and if we aren’t willing to risk something new, our spark crumbles and breaks down. 

No matter what phase i’m in—the building or the breaking, I know that if I step into a studio, I am home. Home in this body, home in this world. 

If any of you are asking yourselves where your spark for life went- ask: have I abandoned parts of myself? Go backwards. Sometimes, (most of the time) our evolution comes from peeling back the layers that were never meant to be there. Remembering who you were is how you continue to build your legacy, staying forever faithful to your spark. Our childhood dreams become our adult passions.

description:
SAVE THIS☝🏽for your next Push Day
These were the exercises I did to unlock SUPERHUMAN Pushing Strength.
Comment SUPERHUMAN & I’ll send you the full video breakdown 🔓

Each exercise has an easier progression to scale:
1.  Incline Pseudo Push Ups -  pseudo push ups
2. 90* Toe Taps - 90* pumps
3. Half Lay to 90* Hold - Push Up to 90* Hold
4. Assisted Tuck Planche Push Ups - Tuck Planche Push Ups
5. Jumping Lean Dips - Lean Dips

Doing these exercises while leaning forward as far as you can is going to allow you to advance through the progressions & eventually develop your strength to push from your waistline, which is required to perform Full Planche Push Ups & to lift your body off the ground horizontally. If it’s your first time, try with a resistance band, you may have better results 🤟🏽🖤 (i have them available on @thenx .com/shop)

Not only are these exercises great for achieving the Full Planche Push Up, they’re also very effective at developing the muscles in your core and the majority of your upper body responsible for pushing like your Chest, Triceps, shoulders, and even your Rhomboids, Lower Back, Biceps, lats, traps,  Brachialis, & Brachioradialis.

For more advanced athletes, do these exercises with a @weightvest your reps and strength will greatly increase really fast.

THE WORKOUT:
Work your way up the progressions with a couple reps & sets each.

You can also start with the hardest progression you’re capable of doing and going for 1 or more reps every minute on the minute until you break form, then repeat down the progressional tree.

If this was my workout for the day I’d finish off with a couple sets of weighted Push Ups,
& Weighted Dips

Hope this helps!💪🏽

title:
About a decade ago, people said you shouldn’t let your knees go past your toes when you squat.

Why? Because it increases stress on the knees.

But stress on your knees isn’t bad. It is literally part
description:
About a decade ago, people said you shouldn’t let your knees go past your toes when you squat.

Why? Because it increases stress on the knees.

But stress on your knees isn’t bad. It is literally part of squatting. Adding weight to the bar also increases knee stress, yet nobody argues we should avoid that.

Knee valgus is similar, and the fitness industry may just need some time to digest that instead of inherently fearing it.

In an experienced lifter, some degree of knee valgus is often a strength strategy that can improve performance, not something you need to fear or automatically correct.

It can help you use your adductors more effectively, improve length tension relationships in the hip extensors, and create stronger force production out of the bottom.

The goal isn’t zero stress.

The goal is having tissues that are strong enough for the stress you choose.

Context matters.

Beginner with poor control and pain? Different conversation.
Experienced lifter moving heavy weight with no symptoms? Often normal.

Don’t confuse exposure with danger.

title: Isometrics can build just as much muscle as full range training. A recent study comparing full range knee extensions to lengthened isometric holds found similar hypertrophy (PMID 40911904). Earlier re
description:
Isometrics can build just as much muscle as full range training. A recent study comparing full range knee extensions to lengthened isometric holds found similar hypertrophy (PMID 40911904). Earlier research shows the same pattern (PMID 3443943, 15075307).

But not all isometrics are created equal. When studies compare long versus short muscle length isometrics, longer positions tend to produce more growth. The same pattern appears with dynamic reps.

Most lifters understand the importance of challenging muscles at longer lengths, or at least training through a full range of motion, which usually ensures this. However, many popular calisthenics isometrics are performed in relatively short positions, such as the planche, front lever, touch front lever, or a chin up hold at the top. These exercises are excellent for building strength at specific joint angles. That is their main purpose. They still provide a hypertrophy stimulus, but compared to dynamic alternatives like planche push ups, front lever raises, or chin ups, they would likely underperform for muscle growth.

Some isometrics challenge muscles at longer lengths, such as the bent arm planche, back lever, human flag, dragon flag hold, or a deep wall sit. Because these load muscles in more lengthened positions, they likely perform similarly to dynamic alternatives for hypertrophy.

One more misconception - Long is better than short for growth, but longer is not always better than long. When research compares long to very long muscle lengths, hypertrophy is usually similar and sometimes even favors slightly less extreme ranges. For example, push ups bringing your chest to the floor already create a meaningful stretch in the pecs. Elevating your hands for more depth probably does not increase growth and may reduce how much load you can handle.

In summary, I use isometrics primarily to build strength in specific positions. Short position isometrics are fantastic for positional strength and still build some muscle. But if hypertrophy is your main goal, dynamic reps or lengthened isometrics are likely the better choice. Pausing in the stretched portion of a rep can also combine both stimuli.

title: Whether or not you’re aware it, your spine is flexing under load every time you train heavy squats and deadlifts. Not just a bit either! When doing heavy deadlifts, the spine flexes to about 70-80% or
description:
Whether or not you’re aware it, your spine is flexing under load every time you train heavy squats and deadlifts. Not just a bit either! When doing heavy deadlifts, the spine flexes to about 70-80% or maximal flexion range! Even when the back appears neutral or lordotic, it’s still flexing significantly every time you hinge at the hips (PMID: 33799053).

Not only is spinal flexion under load unavoidable, it happens all the time in sports like rowing, wrestling, and football. Yet in these high-contact scenarios, no one panics.

But in the gym — the safest, most controlled environment, where you choose the load and progression — people act like a bit of spinal flexion will make your back explode 🤦‍♂️

You’ll be far more prepared for spinal flexion under load if you progressively expose yourself to it.

Want a resilient back? Strengthen it
Want a fragile back? Neglect it

title:
Why do longer arms make the front lever easier? 

If your center of mass sits the same distance from the shoulder, the torque should be identical… so difficulty should be identical too. Right?

Wrong.
description:
Why do longer arms make the front lever easier? 

If your center of mass sits the same distance from the shoulder, the torque should be identical… so difficulty should be identical too. Right?

Wrong. 

Arm length does not change the external torque. It changes the joint angle your shoulder extensors have to work in. Shorter arms force you into more acute shoulder flexion. Longer arms keep you closer to where the shoulder extensors produce their highest torque (60 to 100 degrees of shoulder flexion).

Same external load. 
Different internal mechanics. 
Different strength potential. 

Think about holding a dumbbell straight out in front of you while standing. Now lie prone and try to hold it in the same horizontal position. The torque equation is identical, but one feels brutally harder. That is joint angle and muscle length at work. 

Short arms will not ruin your front lever. But they do shift you further from the shoulder’s strongest range. You cannot change your arm length, so build the strength your structure demands.

Happy training 💪

description:
Three tips for learning the rings muscle-up

1. Use a false grip

This puts your hands in the correct position to support yourself once you reach the dip. Without it, your wrists end up overly extended and in an awkward position.

2. Get good at high chin-ups

The transition is the hardest part of the skill. If you can minimize the distance of the transition, the muscle-up becomes much easier. Build this strength by doing paused chin-ups and holding the rings to your chest at the top of each rep.

3. Keep the rings close

Letting the rings drift away during the transition turns the movement into more of an iron cross raise than a dip.

title:
Knee valgus, aka knee cave, shows up in beginners and elite lifters alike. So why does it happen in the squat?

Sometimes it’s a limitation:

- poor motor control

- a strategy to compensate for restr
description:
Knee valgus, aka knee cave, shows up in beginners and elite lifters alike. So why does it happen in the squat?

Sometimes it’s a limitation:

- poor motor control

- a strategy to compensate for restricted ankle range of motion

Other times, it’s just your body maximizing performance. The adductor magnus and glutes work together to extend the hips, with the adductor magnus doing more in deep squat positions. When it contracts, it can pull the knees inward.

Allowing the knees to cave can put these muscles at their ideal lengths to generate force. It can change moment arms, reduce knee extensor demands, and shift load to the hips.

A 2024 study (PMID: 38416444) compared squats with knees in, out, or neutral:

knees in: less demand on adductors, more on glutes and lateral rotators

knees out: more demand on adductors, less on glutes

This challenges the usual narrative. Knee cave is often blamed on weak glutes, but this suggests the opposite. Knees in might indicate stronger glutes relative to adductors, while knees out could reflect stronger adductors and relatively weaker glutes.

Knee cave is not always a flaw. Sometimes it’s just your body choosing the strongest path to move weight. 

Oh, and knee valgus is generally very safe in the barbell squat. Squats aren’t a highly dynamic movement that carry risk of ACL tears. Those almost never happen unless something goes drastically wrong. If it feels comfortable, there’s no need to fight knee valgus or drastically change your technique. Elite lifters have been squatting this way for decades and setting world records with it safely.

title: As the name suggests, the quadriceps are made up of four muscles. The VMO, or vastus medialis obliquus, is the part of the quads that looks like a teardrop. It sits on the inside of the knee and is no
description:
As the name suggests, the quadriceps are made up of four muscles. The VMO, or vastus medialis obliquus, is the part of the quads that looks like a teardrop. It sits on the inside of the knee and is not a separate muscle. It is simply the distal portion of the vastus medialis.

Many people blame knee pain on muscular imbalances or a weak VMO. However, this idea relies on assumptions that are not supported by evidence.

• There is no isolated atrophy of the VMO in people with knee pain
• There are no isolated reductions in VMO activity in people with knee pain
• There is no exercise that preferentially increases VMO activity
• Even if there were, EMG is a poor proxy for long term muscle growth

In people with knee pain, research consistently shows general quadriceps atrophy, not isolated VMO atrophy (PMID: 24175596).

EMG findings are highly variable. Some studies show reduced activity in both the VL and VMO in people with knee pain. Others show no difference compared to pain free controls (PMID: 17549952). Some even show greater VMO activity in those with knee pain (PMID: 31453558). Taken in isolation, that last finding could suggest VMO activity should be reduced rather than increased.

There is no practical way to assess VMO strength, or even the vastus medialis alone. All four quadriceps extend the knee, and you cannot isolate one muscle to test it. MRI can assess individual quadriceps size, but this is expensive and impractical.

Attempts to preferentially target the VMO with specific exercises have failed (PMID: 19212898). All quadriceps work together. Even if an exercise increased VMO activity, that would not guarantee greater VMO hypertrophy, as EMG does not predict long term muscle growth (PMID: 35006527).

If you want healthy knees, strengthen the quads through a full ROM, use varied exercises, train the hips and legs, and load the quads at longer muscle lengths.

Send this to someone who still calls exercises “VMO step ups” or “VMO squats”.
author: simonsterstrength

title: I think everyone should be able to control their knee position when squatting with light loads. However, if you have good control and your knees only move inward as the weight gets heavy, that is abso
description:
I think everyone should be able to control their knee position when squatting with light loads. However, if you have good control and your knees only move inward as the weight gets heavy, that is absolutely fine.

The body often adopts this pattern because it is stronger. Actively avoiding it would usually reduce how much weight you can lift. The clips shown are of world record squatters, and this knee movement may occur for several reasons, such as optimizing the length of the adductor magnus and glutes to maximize force production, or shifting some load toward stronger muscle groups. The adductor magnus is one of the primary muscles responsible for extending the hip from the bottom of a squat. It could also just be this muscle pulling the knee in as it works to extend the hip.

This is not a pattern everyone has. Some people are stronger without knee valgus, and this comes down to individual characteristics like anatomy and the relative strength of contributing muscles.

If knee injury is the concern, the squat is extremely safe. It is a controlled movement, not a highly dynamic task involving jumping, twisting, and rapid deceleration, which is how most ACL injuries actually occur.

People used to fear knees traveling past the toes, yet we now know that is perfectly fine. Olympic lifters have always squatted this way. The same principle applies to knee valgus. If it feels fine and you have control over knee position with submaximal loads, there’s no need to avoid valgus or change your technique.

title:
There are many ways to progressively overload an exercise. With most pushing exercises, one option is adjusting the height of the parallettes.

Sometimes, increasing the height makes an exercise harde
description:
There are many ways to progressively overload an exercise. With most pushing exercises, one option is adjusting the height of the parallettes.

Sometimes, increasing the height makes an exercise harder by increasing the range of motion the muscles work through. For example, handstand push-ups become deeper and more demanding on taller parallettes.

Other times, increasing the height actually reduces difficulty. This can happen by inclining the body, as in push-ups, or by giving the legs more room to move, such as during L-sit to push-up transitions. Height can also change lever arms and the length at which muscles work, making certain skills easier. For example, a bent-arm handstand, often called a shoulder stand, is much easier on tall parallettes where the head can sit lower. On low parallettes, you must push much higher with the upper arms close to horizontal just to keep the head off the ground. This increases the lever arms of resistance at the shoulder and significantly increases the difficulty.

Happy training

description:
Give your brain a breather.
This 60-second digital reset with Yoga With Adrien’s @adrienelouise is designed to soothe screen fatigue, calm your nervous system, and help you come back to yourself.

👁 Soften your gaze—or gently close your eyes
🧠 Picture a place or person that brings you joy
🌬️ Take a slow, steady inhale
🌀 Return to your surroundings with care
✨ Breathe. Notice what shifts.

Whether you’re scattered, overwhelmed, or just need a break from the scroll—this moment is yours.

Where did your mind go during that reset?
A quiet beach? A forest with owls? A cozy couch with someone you love?

👇 Drop your answer in the comments—or just leave an emoji that captures the vibe.
💬 Tag someone who could use a screen break today.

📩 Share this in your stories as a reminder to pause.
—

description:
It’s actually kind of cute 
And somewhat of a full circle style kind of perfect 
That I write to you from on my yoga mat, 
Mexican blankets to cushion, blocks clumped together 
To serve as a desk. 

In Yoga Therapy school, but also in an old church, in study, but also just with me, being me, the way one does on the yoga mat.
 
After weeks of travel, back in Austin. 
After a year of preparing our house to make it home, 
we are now in the final stretch. 

After a tumultuous election week in my country, still in the midst of processing, the heart aches and the sun shines, both at the same time. 
 
The temptation to spiral is strong. 
And yet, so many things whisper... 
Come back Adriene, come back. 

Then I realize it’s time for a new release -  from my heart to yours, seeming to come at what feels like divine time.

Turn The Page Meditation awaits you. ✨

Meet me by the stream. It is 16 min. 

Make time for it, for you, to sit, to breathe, to shift and turn towards what matters most at this time. 
 
What that is, only you will know. 

So, listen to your heart. 

With Love, 
 Adriene 

Love letter in your box with the practice link. Also find it free on YouTube, or on our beloved find what feels good app - where our 7 day meditation challenge kicks off today. Booyah. I’ll meet you there!

All you need is 20min 🫶🏼

🔥SUPERSET A (6min):
10 reverse lunges 
10 squat to shoulder press

💧60s rest

🔥SUPERSET B (6min):
5 push ups
10 narrow shoulder press

💧60s rest 

🔥SUPERSET C (6min):
10 seated above bicycles
10 leg lowers

Postpartum has been a whole different ballgame.
A journey of acceptance and also coming back to myself a
description:
Because it really is that deep.
Pregnancy was the first time I felt like a stranger in my body.
Postpartum has been a whole different ballgame.
A journey of acceptance and also coming back to myself at the same time. While not rushing anything.

I promised myself that I wouldn’t leave myself behind when I became a mum.

At the beginning of this chapter, 16 weeks ago… I felt so overwhelmed by the mountain I felt like I had to climb in front of me.
I’ve never met this version of me before.
This was navigating new territory.
I have never tried to work on any goals with another human completely dependent on me.
Could I do it? Was it possible? 
But I made a promise… That I would make time for the things that help me feel like me.
Working out.
Getting my nails done.
Having facials.
Whatever it was.
Carving out the time I do have for me and making it count.

This was never about getting my body back.
It’s about me feeling confident in my own skin.
Feeling like myself again, little by little.
And there’s nothing wrong with wanting to become the strongest and most confident version you can be.
For yourself.
Not for anyone else but you.
Here’s to continuing that process, of enjoying being a work in progress.
One day at a time 🤍

Now this is a tricky one and I actually
description:
I promised myself that when I became a mum, I wouldn’t leave myself behind. That I would still do things for me, that I would still have goals to work towards.

Now this is a tricky one and I actually have been struggling to articulate what I want to say because I don’t want it to come across wrong. So here it goes…

I have a lot of goals. 
Some I have achieved, like running 57 miles in memory of my Dad.
Some that I have yet to bring to life.
Some that I am currently working on at the moment.
They come in all different shapes, sizes and intensities.

You can’t do it all, not when you become a mum.
And nor should I be able to. 
That’s not what this season of life is about.
That time will come again one day I’m sure.
But… My priorities have shifted completely.
I can’t go out and run a marathon on a Sunday morning or spend hours perfecting my handstands like I used to.
And I am more than okay with that.
There’s plenty I still CAN work on and focus on.

There are still goals I can go after that allow me to work on myself and be a mum at the same time. That fit this chapter beautifully and fill my cup up.

It doesn’t have to be one or the other.
But it has to be realistic.
Your goals have to meet you where you are in life.
Or you’ll just be frustrated and disappointed.

So these goals I have might not be as extreme or as extravagant as before, but they are just as meaningful and just as important to me.

Becoming a mum, for me, means working on my goals while being the best and most present parent I can be.

And I hope I can show our baby girl that she deserves to prioritize things that are important to her.

description:
6 hours after giving birth vs. 6 weeks postpartum🤰🏻 

There was nothing magic I did, no crazy dieting, no working out… Just gentle walks and pelvic floor, deep core work and breathing exercises.

6 weeks of letting my body heal, on its own timeline, not the worlds. 

For me, postpartum was never about “getting my body back”

It’s been a season of slowing down.
Taking the pressure off.
Adapting and learning how to step into my new role as a mum.

If you are pregnant or just gave birth, I hope that this helps you navigate this chapter in a way that looks after YOU.

I am so excited to be able to build back up over the next few months because I gave my body the chance to recover, to reset and to heal.

Your body will do exactly what it needs to do to create life and how to heal after bringing that life into this world. 🙏🏼

title: I don’t know how to explain it, but since becoming a Mum (still feels wild to say that), I find myself caught between moments having this thought of “I’m going to miss this so much” before the moment
description:
I don’t know how to explain it, but since becoming a Mum (still feels wild to say that), I find myself caught between moments having this thought of “I’m going to miss this so much” before the moment is over or done. 

I have spent hours and hours memorizing her little face and the way her little body felt laying on my chest. 
The little noises she’d make while I’d feed her. 
Thinking… “I have to take this in, I have to.” 
Because everyone kept telling me how quickly it would go. And it does.

Truthfully, it made it hard to accept how fast she was changing and how fast the weeks were going by. 
I cried a lot thinking that she wouldn’t be this small forever. 
Which sounds crazy?

But you know, I saw someone speak about this the other day. The whole “blink and you’ll miss it” feeling and sentiment. How it makes us anxious in a moment because we know it’s fleeting and won’t last forever. 

She re-worded it to “be here, right now”. 
So that’s what I’ve been trying to do. 
Sitting in each moment with her, as often as I can. 
Not thinking about anything else. 

She’s growing so fast and what a privilege it is to see her grow and start to see the beginnings of her little personality coming through. 
Her little voice, desperately trying to speak to us, her little smile when she sees us. 
The little nose scrunch she does just before she coo’s.
The way her eyes now follow us.
The way they light up, full of life and excitement.
How she looks around, taking in the world a little more each day.

I’m now beginning to understand that this whole being a Mum thing is not for the weak, a balance between loving and letting go of all of their different versions.

Each one so special, so unique and ever-changing ❤️

title: I know what I would say if one of our 1:1 girls felt like this after giving birth. I’d tell her to be kinder to herself, to give herself and her body grace after bringing life into this world. That sh
description:
I know what I would say if one of our 1:1 girls felt like this after giving birth. I’d tell her to be kinder to herself, to give herself and her body grace after bringing life into this world. That she has done the most incredible thing and recovery takes time.

I’d remind her that these feelings are valid but that they are also temporary. That she won’t feel this way forever. That she is not alone.

I’d tell her that together, we’d build up her strength again. That she’d be able to do what she used to before and more. That if she gave herself the time and the consistency, it will pay off. 

I would say that yes, her goals feel so very far away right now and it’s overwhelming and in some ways feels impossible. I would gently let her know that they might feel like that for some time, until they’re not, and the progress starts becoming visible. 

That this is where trusting the process matters most.

And finally I’d remind her that progress takes time, it’s not going to happen overnight. 
But you know what? 
That time is going to pass regardless. 
So why not spend it trying. 
Why not see what your body can do. 
What your mind can do. 
Why not?

So if you are feeling like I am right now, this one’s for you, for us, for any mama navigating new territory. 
You are not alone and this is where we rebuild, in a way we never have had to before. 

Come and sign up for 1:1 coaching with me and our incredible team who are here to help support you through your movement journey no matter what chapter you are on 🌱 www.11coaching.co.uk

title:
2 months of our beautiful Olivia 🩷

I would be lying if I said I hadn’t been a little scared to have a newborn. They call it the “newborn trenches” and for the entire duration of my pregnancy I heard
description:
2 months of our beautiful Olivia 🩷

I would be lying if I said I hadn’t been a little scared to have a newborn. They call it the “newborn trenches” and for the entire duration of my pregnancy I heard a lot of “just you wait”. You get told all of the stories about how hard it is, how sleep deprived it is and how your life is never truly yours again. 

Perhaps that is true for some but what they don’t tell you often enough is that yes it’s hard, yes you will sleep less and yes your life is no longer just yours, but in the most incredible, special and life changing way imaginable.

So much so that I would do anything to be able to go back and spend just a little longer in those moments.

Meeting her for the first time.
Holding her for the first time.
That first cry.
Her little newborn scrunch.
The milk drunk pouts.
The countless middle of the night feeds where it was just her and I.
Nothing to do.
No where to be.
But right there with her.

When they tell you that it goes by quickly, believe them.
I blinked… and we are here, 8 weeks on. 
The best 8 weeks of our life.

Learning how to love and let go of these versions of her is something I never even contemplated before.

All I know is that I’ve been on this earth for 32 years before I met her and I only just feel like I’ve truly started living now 🩷

title:
I’ve seen so much online about how women change when they become a mum. 
As if they are somehow surprised and simultaneously disappointed?
I’m surprised people are surprised, but at the same time, unt
description:
I’ve seen so much online about how women change when they become a mum. 
As if they are somehow surprised and simultaneously disappointed?
I’m surprised people are surprised, but at the same time, until you have been pregnant and birthed a baby, it’s hard to understand.
I didn’t quite grasp just how much this would change me, for the better.
How it would re-wire my very being.
Shift my perspective entirely.
Completely change my priorities in every single way possible.
It unlocks a version of you that you never knew existed.
The capacity to love in a way you never imagined.
A beautiful and efficient filtration system that weeds out what matters and what ultimately doesn’t.
So, yes I have completely changed in so many ways.
Yet I am still me in other ways.
A meeting of different parts of myself.
A letting go of the parts no longer needed.
I look in the mirror and I see them all coming together in their own messy way.
I look in the mirror and I’m proud of who I was and who I am becoming.
How could I not love this version of me? 
It created her. ❤️
author: jessicaolie

title: I have seen so many posts and conversations on the internet with the messaging something along the lines of “how to lose weight while breastfeeding” and the first thing it made me feel was pressure an
description:
I have seen so many posts and conversations on the internet with the messaging something along the lines of “how to lose weight while breastfeeding” and the first thing it made me feel was pressure and the second thing it made me feel was sad.

I have chosen to breastfeed my baby not for anything else but for HER health and I am so grateful that I am able to exclusively breastfeed.

My body is literally sustaining her right now. 
I am her only source of food. 
Her ability to be nourished is my responsibility and there is absolutely no way that I would ever want to jeopardize that…
Just so I can fit into my pre-pregnancy clothes?

There will be a time where I can be in a calorie deficit if I choose, but losing weight is not my priority right now, feeding my baby is.

title:
When you want to workout but your b00bie is required, you need to be quick & effective 🤭

I am currently exclusively breastfeeding and I knew committing to that would mean that my body would be requir
description:
When you want to workout but your b00bie is required, you need to be quick & effective 🤭

I am currently exclusively breastfeeding and I knew committing to that would mean that my body would be required on demand by Olivia, whether it was convenient or not 🤍

Sometimes she will nap for 90 minutes, sometimes it’s closer to 30 minutes. So I do what I can. 

The most important thing I feel like everyone needs to hear, is that it’s not about quantity… it’s about quality and intensity. 

This workout consisted of 3 key movements and I promise you, you do not need to do 6, 7 or 8 different exercises to get results. I usually do 4-5 exercises on lower body day if I have the time.

So if you are short on time, make the most out of the time you have. Even if it’s not the full workout, it’s always better done than left for a “perfect” day.

I hope you can see that this journey doesn’t require us to be perfect but it does require us to show up and that might look different week to week.

description:
2 weeks postpartum and I just keep thinking how incredible our bodies are.

During my pregnancy my weight was a frequent topic of discussion, I gained over 20kg by the time I gave birth and while I have yet to step on the scales (because I don’t care) you can see that my body knew exactly what it needed to do to grow our baby girl. 

I am focusing on nourishing my body as much as I can to heal.
Sleeping when I can to help my body recover (but that’s hard with a newborn)
Walking here and there to get some light movement in.

I had SO many messages from women during the course of my pregnancy saying they were worried about getting pregnant because of what it would do to their body.

So I hope by sharing my PP journey you can see that our bodies are so clever, we are literally designed for this. 

Your body will do exactly what it needs to do to grow your baby and that will look so different on everyone. 

Please don’t compare your journey or your body to anyone else’s, not ever but especially when you are creating life (read that again) ❤️ 

#postpartum #pregnancy

title:
Ugh our bodies are just amazing 😩 2 days postpartum vs. 4 weeks postpartum🤰🏻 

I promised I’d share my postpartum journey and just like pregnancy, I honestly had no idea what to expect, how my recover
description:
Ugh our bodies are just amazing 😩 2 days postpartum vs. 4 weeks postpartum🤰🏻 

I promised I’d share my postpartum journey and just like pregnancy, I honestly had no idea what to expect, how my recovery would feel, how I would feel within myself and how long it would begin to take to *start* to feel like myself again.

I am by no means where I was before I got pregnant, duh 😂
And it’s okay to look like you’ve had a baby after you’ve had a baby, period.
I cannot emphasize that enough.
My body is still healing.
My belly is still softer.
But I’m not rushing anything.

And whenever I think perhaps I should look different, I gently remind myself that 4 weeks ago I just pushed an entire human out of my body.
And how incredible that is.

I have a long way to build back up to where I was but as I journey through this new chapter I feel less drawn to try go back to who I was before I got pregnant and more called to step into this new version of me & this new version of my body.
Getting to know her.
Giving her grace.
Making sure I don’t compare myself or my recovery to anyone else’s. I think that’s so important.
We are all on our own journey and timeline.
And most of all giving myself the freedom to see what this season holds for me and my fitness journey as a Mummy.
author: jessicaolie

title: I shared my pregnancy journey as honestly and openly as I could and my intention is to do the same postpartum. From growing her for 9 months, to her making her arrival earth side, I am so proud of my
description:
I shared my pregnancy journey as honestly and openly as I could and my intention is to do the same postpartum. From growing her for 9 months, to her making her arrival earth side, I am so proud of my body and the journey it’s been through.

To go from being her home on the inside to her home on the outside in a different way. 

In a world where “bounce back” culture still exists, I am in no rush to return to the body I had before. 
There is no going back to who I was, physically or mentally. 
There is only moving forwards, to become the strongest I can be for me but also for her, in time.

I am in awe of what our bodies can do.
Create life.
Sustain life.
Stretch.
Expand.
Like breathing air.
How could I ever not love the body she called home for so long?
That grew her?
That nourished her?

Brick by brick I will build up slowly, except now, with a quiet strength and confidence knowing that if my body could do that? 
It can do anything.

❤️

description:
Tending to bees has become a true highlight of my life. Sharing it with my little ones makes it even more special🧡 

It’s early May and still freezing at night here but the bees are doing amazing! The hive was filled with honey and brood and just bursting with life. There was a single frame filled to the brim with perfectly capped honey - felt like such a gift🥹 

I am much less hands-on with the bees these days than I was when I was first learning; now instead of controlling and inspecting all the time I try to give them as much space as possible and let them lead. Building a swarm hive out of a hollow tree trunk now and hoping to capture my first swarm this season (let’s see how that goes!!) 🐝 

Have you ever seen the inside of a beehive? And did you know that 100% of non-Swedish honey tested on the shelves here in Sweden turned out not to be honey at all? Always get your honey locally, from real beekeepers! #beehive #beekeeper #honey #bees

title:
Realizing that no one is coming to save me could have been a terrifying thing… but actually, it was liberating. 

I guess I can finally say I’m a prepper now🤷‍♀️ if the zombie apocalypse happens tomor
description:
Realizing that no one is coming to save me could have been a terrifying thing… but actually, it was liberating. 

I guess I can finally say I’m a prepper now🤷‍♀️ if the zombie apocalypse happens tomorrow (or something less unlikely say an energy collapse or world war 3 or another pandemic or a shutdown of any of the incredibly fragile systems we rely so deeply on in our day to day) - we’ll be ok. I have gone from thinking crisis preparedness was a little nutty to wearing my tinfoil hat like a crown😆 I have a 16-point master document covering every area of crisis preparedness; from water to food, first aid, communication, sanitation, health, security… And yes, we have long-term food storage that will cover us for 3+ months (something that takes way more planning than I thought to get right)! Why, you might ask? What am I preparing for? I don’t know! When Covid came along I wish I was a lot more prepared and these days, the world feels on the brink of some sort of collapse in different ways every single day. So I want to have our bases covered (if we wake up tomorrow and the power is down, I want to be able to keep my kids warm and fed!).

I know you either think this is batshit crazy oooor you’ve been thinking about these things and you, too, have realized that if sh*t hits the fan, no one is coming to save you either. It’s up to us to keep our families nourished, comfortable and safe. 

I cover every detail of my prepping on my last two podcast episodes on Patreon if you want to ge yourself a tinfoil tiara and tune in. Comment PREPAREDNESS and this weird little Instagram robot will send you the link! (also, link in bio)👸🚨🔦🧯🦠

title: I’m not going to show you my ugly dance because the whole point is it’s not a performance but seriously - when was the last time you let yourself out of the cage of having to be so fucking palatable a
description:
I’m not going to show you my ugly dance because the whole point is it’s not a performance but seriously - when was the last time you let yourself out of the cage of having to be so fucking palatable all the time?? I think we have generations of witches healers oracles grandmothers behind us urging us to drop the façade and to let our inner witches out. When I’m moving and I’m able to let go completely I sometimes envision my hair turning completely gray, warts growing out of my face, nose hairs long, back crooked… And I just laugh. It’s the best feeling. Being “pretty” is a cage. Fitting in is a cage. Playing small is a cage. For how long have we exhausted ourselves to be beautiful, to be thin, to be acceptable - bending over backwards to not be too much, too loud, to not take up too much space. I’ve spent a lifetime doing that. So when I dance I see Baba Yaga. I see Kali. I feel her. 

In another lifetime I was her!! And I bring her out to play a little bit each time I ugly dance.

You should try it, too🧙‍♀️

#freedom #selfcare #letgo

title: Home with chicken pox (him) and a bad cold (me) and melting together on the yoga mat this morning softened me all the way to my core. When people ask why I still breastfeed, my first answer is usually
description:
Home with chicken pox (him) and a bad cold (me) and melting together on the yoga mat this morning softened me all the way to my core. When people ask why I still breastfeed, my first answer is usually a question in return (why not?) but the next time someone asks maybe I’ll direct them toward this video. 

For connection. 
For nourishment. 
For rest. 
For love. 

This is as quiet as he will be during the day, or ever (he’s pretty wild even in his sleep). Nursing him at 2,5 is a dance I didn’t know we would still be dancing this far postpartum but I’m so glad we still are. For a few moments each day, we are both still. Right here, him and I. Extending the embodied magic of our bond for as long as we can. 

My sun ☀️❤️

#motherhood #breastfeeding #family #selfcare #yoga

title:
Halloween at the farm, 2025 edition👻 

To imagine that this whole thing started with our (then) 7-year old daughter casually inviting over one hundred people to a small halloween gathering at home😆 no
description:
Halloween at the farm, 2025 edition👻 

To imagine that this whole thing started with our (then) 7-year old daughter casually inviting over one hundred people to a small halloween gathering at home😆 now it’s a festival! Halloween isn’t a big celebration in Sweden and something we decided to bring with us when we moved from Aruba (trick or treating was always epic on our street!). Im glad I didn’t have to rent a portapotty in a panic to keep the (surprise!) 110 people who came to our little party last year from using our bathroom😆 @ala_farms will be the place to celebrate Halloween every year from now on (three public bathrooms! a bar! hot coffee! cows!!! and more ghosts haunting the land than you can count…)🧟‍♀️

Thank you to our amazing actors!!! @mattef72 @erik.dahlin.7 @shama_persson @f_anders + to the whole farm team and our family for pulling this off and working so hard with us. And to @ludvig_brathen (who I barely saw all night because he was standing perfectly still in the shadows of a barn waiting for people to approach him before scaring the bejeezus out of every single person visiting)😬😂

We are already counting down the days until next year… who wants to visit 2026??! 🎃❤️ @ala_farms #halloween #farm #hauntedhouse #fall #autumn #spooky #spookyseason

title: A little haunted house tour!! This is a very old house on our land that our daughter has named “The Ghost House” because once in a blue moon, she enters and randomly finds treats inside the old wood s
description:
A little haunted house tour!! This is a very old house on our land that our daughter has named “The Ghost House” because once in a blue moon, she enters and randomly finds treats inside the old wood stove that the ghost has left for her👻  And I swear, sometimes when I walk by I see shadows moving in the window on the top floor. When we first moved to the homestead and I entered this place for the first time there was an empty coffee cup and a newspaper from 1970 open on the kitchen table😳 the place is filled with treasure! It’s been three years and we are finally getting around to cleaning this place out. There is no running water or electricity and properly restoring it is a massive endeavor… My plan for right now is to see if we can get it decent enough to turn it into an art studio (of the ghost allows!!)🩶 

I’ve never shared a reel this long before. Feels like a proper vlog! Follow along for part two (and to see the craziest thing we found up in the attic)…

#hauntedhouse #homestead #homerestoration #ghost #halloween #spooky #renovation #history #sweden #farmlife

description:
If you loved my viral banana coconut cookies, try this version as bars! 
INGREDIENTS
Cooking spray
2 ripe bananas
2 cups unsweetened shredded coconut
2 ounces chocolate bar
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F. Line an 8x8-inch baking pan with parchment paper, leaving some overhang on the sides, then lightly coat with cooking spray.
2. In a large bowl, mash the bananas until mostly smooth. Add the shredded coconut and use a fork to mix until the coconut is fully coated and the mixture holds together.
3. Transfer the banana coconut mixture to the prepared pan. Use a spatula or your hands to press it firmly and evenly into the bottom of the pan.
4. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the top looks set.
5. Immediately break the chocolate bar on top when it’s done baking, allow it to melt for 5 minutes. Then spread evenly over the bars.
6. Refrigerate for 30 minutes, then lift out of the pan and cut into bars.

description:
Here’s a fun way to make scrambled eggs in the oven with feta cheese - #bakedfetaeggs The feta makes it creamy, fluffy and so good! 🍳
INGREDIENTS
Avocado oil spray
8 ounce block feta cheese
12 eggs
2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil
¼ teaspoon salt
¼ teaspoon black pepper
Fresh mint leaves, for serving
Pita bread, for serving
INSTRUCTIONS
1. Preheat oven to 400°F. Grease an 8x11 baking dish.
2. Place the feta block in the middle of the prepared baking dish. Crack 12 eggs around the feta cheese. Drizzle the olive oil on top of the feta and eggs. Season the eggs with salt. Season the eggs and feta with the black pepper. 
3. Bake in the preheated oven for 18-22 minutes, until the feta cheese melts and the egg whites around the cook.
4. Use a fork to scramble the eggs and feta together. Don’t worry if some of the whites still look wet as they will continue cooking from the heat of the baking dish and surrounding eggs.
5. Enjoy the eggs alone or scoop into pita bread with mint leaves to make a sandwich.

INGREDIENTS3 cups cooked short
description:
If you’re bored of chicken and rice, try baking your rice in a muffin tin to make crispy little rice cups instead – I stuffed mine with teriyaki chicken! IB: ems.eats

INGREDIENTS3 cups cooked short-grain rice
Cooking spray
¼ cup soy sauce
3 tablespoons packed light brown sugar
4 tablespoons water, divided
1 tablespoon rice vinegar
1 tablespoon toasted sesame oil
1 tablespoon grated fresh ginger
3 garlic cloves, grated
2 teaspoons cornstarch
1 teaspoon sriracha
1 tablespoon avocado oil
1 pound boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1-inch cubes
INSTRUCTIONS
1.	Preheat the oven to 425°F. Grease a 12-cup muffin tin well.
2.	Divide the cooked rice between the muffin cups. Spray with cooking spray Use the back of a spoon or a small measuring cup to firmly press the rice into the bottom and up the sides of each cup. 
3.	Bake for 20-25 minutes,until the rice cups are golden and crisp around the edges, 20 to 25 minutes.
4.	While the rice cups bake, make the sauce. In a medium bowl, whisk together the soy sauce, brown sugar, 2 tablespoons water, rice vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, garlic, cornstarch, and sriracha.
5.	Heat the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook, stirring often, until browned and cooked through, 7 to 8 minutes.
6.	Pour the sauce into the skillet with the chicken and cook until thickened and glossy, about 2 minutes. Add the broccoli and toss to combine.
7.	Fill each rice cup with the chicken mixture. Garnish with greens and toasted sesame seeds before serving.

description:
Low carb Lebanese meat pies using rice paper rolls! 🙌
INGREDIENTS
2 tablespoons olive oil
1 medium onion, diced
1 pound 95% lean ground beef
2 Roma tomatoes, seeded and finely chopped
¼ cup finely chopped fresh parsley
1 teaspoon salt
2 teaspoons 7 Spice
2 teaspoons sumac
½ teaspoon cinnamon
12–14 round rice paper sheets
Olive oil spray
INSTRUCTIONS
1.	Heat the olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat. Add the diced onion and cook until soft and translucent, about 8–10 minutes. Add the ground beef and cook, breaking it apart, until browned and fully cooked through, about 8–10 minutes.
2.	Stir in the tomatoes and parsley. Season with salt, 7 Spice, sumac, and cinnamon. Cook for 2–3 more minutes until everything is well combined and most of the moisture has evaporated. Remove from heat and let the mixture cool slightly.
3.	Fill a shallow dish with warm water. Dip one rice paper sheet into the water for about 5–7 seconds until just pliable
4.	Place it on a clean surface. Spoon about 2-3 tablespoons of the meat mixture in the middle, fold 4 times to make a square. Repeat with another layer of rice paper, then transfer in a single layer to the air fryer.
5.	Lightly spray the top of the meat pies. Air Fry 400°F for 8–12 minutes, until golden brown and crispy. Let cool slightly to crisp more before serving.

description:
(ad) CONTEST Want to win $1,000 AND a year’s supply of Red Gold Tomatoes? If so, listen up!

The Red Gold Challenge is officially back and better than ever. Don’t miss your chance to join in on the fun!

I recently took the @redgoldtomatoes challenge to compare their whole canned tomatoes with a nationwide brand, and the difference was clear. The color, shape, firmness, and rich red juice stood out immediately. It easily scored 5/5 on my scorecard. I used them to make a Marry Me Tomato Orzo, and it feels good putting high-quality ingredients on the table for my family.

TO ENTER:
Follow @redgoldtomatoes + @thefeedfeed
Like this post
Comment and tag a friend (more comments = more entries!)

Contest closes June 30, 2026 at 11:59pm. All valid entries must be submitted prior. Let the challenge commence!

✨Marry Me Tomato Orzo✨

INGREDIENTS
2 tablespoons olive oil, divided
1 (15-ounce) can chickpeas, drained, rinsed, and patted dry
1 teaspoon Italian seasoning, divided
1 teaspoon paprika
3/4 teaspoon salt, divided
1/2 teaspoon black pepper, divided
3 garlic cloves, minced
1 (28-ounce) can Red Gold Whole Peeled Tomatoes
2 cups vegetable or chicken stock
1 cup dry orzo
1/2 cup heavy cream
1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional)
1/4 cup chopped fresh basil, plus more for serving

INSTRUCTIONS
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chickpeas and season. Cook 8-10 minutes until crisp and golden. Remove and set aside.

In the same skillet, heat remaining olive oil over medium heat. Add garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in crushed tomatoes, stock, orzo, Italian seasoning, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to medium-low. Cook 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until orzo is tender and liquid is mostly absorbed.

Stir in heavy cream and Parmesan. Cook 1-2 minutes until creamy. Remove from heat and stir in basil. Serve topped with crispy chickpeas and more basil.

title:
Unpopular Opinion: You SHOULDN’T wash your chicken! 🙅🏼‍♀️

Rinsing raw chicken just splashes bacteria around your sink, counters, dishes… you. 🤢 It increases the risk for cross contamination and does
description:
Unpopular Opinion: You SHOULDN’T wash your chicken! 🙅🏼‍♀️

Rinsing raw chicken just splashes bacteria around your sink, counters, dishes… you. 🤢 It increases the risk for cross contamination and does NOTHING to improve the texture, flavor, or moisture content.

The only thing that will kill bacteria is HEAT!

To properly and safely cook your chicken:
Pat dry, season or marinate, and cook until your chicken reaches an internal temp of 165°F 🌡️

If you don’t want to spend the rest of your night sanitizing the entire kitchen, DON’T WASH YOUR CHICKEN ❌

description:
10-Min Mediterranean Sardine Dip 🐟🧠
My husband eats sardines for breakfast every day, and honestly? He’s onto something. I grew up eating them in the Mediterranean, but I know the “fishy” taste can be a dealbreaker. This recipe is how I jazz them up into a 10-minute powerhouse meal that actually tastes incredible.
Consider this your invitation to Mediterranean Nonna vibes—simple, fresh, and intentionally healthy. By using lemon and sumac to cut the oil, you get a bright, briny dip that’s perfect for a Mediterranean Girl Summer lunch.
Ingredients you need to make it:
• Sardines packed in olive oil
• Lemon (zest and juice)
• Dijon mustard
• Sumac
• Ground coriander
• Kosher salt and black pepper
• Shallot
• Carrot
• Fresh herbs (parsley, cilantro, or mint)
• Extra virgin olive oil
• Pita chips for serving
Why everyone is calling sardines “magic”:
• Brain Power: High levels of Omega-3s (DHA/EPA) support memory and focus.
• Mood Support: Packed with Vitamin D to help regulate your mood.
• Natural Energy: One of the few food sources of natural creatine for cellular energy.
• Bone Health: More calcium than a cup of milk and rich in phosphorus.
• Low Mercury: Since they’re small, they are much cleaner than larger predatory fish.

‼️Want the recipe? Comment “recipe” below and I’ll send it to your DMs!

• Muscle & Energy: As I mentioned in the voiceover, sardines are a rare whole-food source of natural creatine, supporting muscle health and cellular energy (Source: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine).

I’ve been struggling with this lately.

description:
One of the things I miss most about living on the Mediterranean is the feeling that it’s actually okay (even expected) to do nothing sometimes.

I’ve been struggling with this lately. 

For me, sitting still often feels more stressful than staying busy. Why do we feel anxious just sitting for a cup of coffee without reaching for our phones or working on a to do list? 

I’m realizing this sweet Italian concept of Dolce Far Niente is far deeper than an aesthetic of a lovely vacation. And it has nothing to do with laziness. 

We know that research shows we’re more productive and creative when we let our brains reset. 

I keep thinking about how much more fruitful my  life would be if I just carved out a few quiet minutes every day. 

Growing up on the Mediterranean, we didn’t have a term for “slow living.” But it felt more natural to pause sometimes. To savor what we work hard for. To be in community with others. And to also be alone. 

Everything works together.

But I’m realizing that maybe sitting fully still is not something I enjoy as much. What fills my cup more is being in the kitchen working on a recipe or just simply playing with ingredients I love. 

Today, I’m finding my stillness making a fresh Panzanella salad—just ripe tomatoes, crusty bread, and plenty of fresh basil. It’s simple, soulful, and exactly what I need to slow down.

I call this my happy gut salad: Mediterranean white bean salad. 🫘✨@themediterraneandish

I lean on beans for my weekly meal prep, and this salad is easily one of my favorites. It’s one of those “non-recipe” recipes that just works every time. When I’m looking for something that tastes fresh but actually keeps me full, this is what I reach for. 

🙌Here is why I love beans:
• Sustained Energy: They’re packed with plant protein and fiber, so you get a steady boost of energy without the mid-day crash.
• Happy Gut: Beans are a powerhouse for your microbiome, helping things stay regular and supporting overall gut health.
• Zero-Effort Prep: No cooking required—just rinse, toss, and you’re done.
• They Love a Marinade: Unlike leafy greens, beans actually taste better the next day after soaking up all that lemon and olive oil.

Ingredients you’ll need:
• White beans (cannellini)
• English cucumber
• Grape or cherry tomatoes
• Green onions
• Fresh parsley
• Fresh mint leaves
• Lemon (zest and juice)
• Salt and pepper
• Za’atar, Sumac, and Aleppo pepper 
• Extra virgin olive oil
• Feta cheese

This mix is simple, bright, and holds up perfectly in the fridge for a few days. 🍋🌿

description:
Do you like one pot meals? 

One pot pastas can be a little tricky, so pause the video for a few tips or see below! 👇🏼

🍅 liquid is your friend! Use tomato juice, broth, or water to cook the pasta. 

🍅 make sure to use a skillet with high sides and a lid. You will need to cover the dish to cook the pasta evenly. 

🍅 check on your pasta often! I like to use tongs to stir every few minutes to make sure it cooks evenly (super important!) and to thicken the liquid with the starches from the pasta. 

One pot pastas are great recipes to master because once you know it you will always have a quick meal to depend on!

title:
Ever notice how an orange (or Ojai Pixie Tangerine) from the fridge tastes more sour than one sitting on the counter?

It’s not your imagination.

Cold temperatures actually make oranges taste less sw
description:
Ever notice how an orange (or Ojai Pixie Tangerine) from the fridge tastes more sour than one sitting on the counter?

It’s not your imagination.

Cold temperatures actually make oranges taste less sweet.

Here’s why.

First—your taste buds work better when food is warmer.

When an orange is really cold, your tongue has a harder time tasting sweetness.

So instead of tasting sweet and juicy…
it tastes flatter and more sour.

Second—most flavor actually comes from smell.

That fresh citrus flavor you love? A lot of that comes from aroma.

When the orange is cold, those smell molecules get trapped inside the fruit.

Less aroma reaches your nose, so the orange tastes less flavorful.

And third—cold can slightly numb your tongue.

Your brain focuses more on the “cold” feeling and less on the actual flavor.

So here’s the trick:
Take your orange out of the fridge and let it sit for about 30 minutes before eating.

Same orange… way better flavor.

Try it once and you’ll never unsee it. 🍊

title: Easy salad idea: load up your favorite veggies on spinach with air fried crispy flax lavash and a creamy tahini dressing. 🥗Lavash flatbread is not only great for rollups and flatbread pizzas, but also
description:
Easy salad idea: load up your favorite veggies on spinach with air fried crispy flax lavash and a creamy tahini dressing. 🥗Lavash flatbread is not only great for rollups and flatbread pizzas, but also toasted to make chips. Here’s how to make it! 

Ingredients👇

For the crispy lavash:
1 @josephsbakery flax lavash bread, cut into strips
½ tsp paprika
1 TBSP olive oil

For the salad & dressing: 
2 beets, chopped
1 TBSP olive oil
1 tsp cumin
Salt & pepper to taste
10 oz spinach, chopped
1 cucumber, chopped
1 carrot, peeled and julienned
½ red onion, chopped small
1 bunch parsley or cilantro, chopped
1 avocado, sliced
1 15 oz can of chickpeas, drained
¾ cup feta crumbles
1/3 cup tahini
Juice from ½ a lemon
2-3 tbsp greek yogurt

Beets: toss the beets on a baking sheet with olive oil, cumin, salt and pepper. Bake at 400 F for 20 minutes, until soft. Stirring halfway is recommended.
Lavash: toss the cut flax lavash bread in a bowl with olive oil, paprika, salt and pepper. Air fry on 390 F for 5 minutes, shaking the basket a few times while cooking. If you don’t have an air fryer, you can add the coated lavash pieces to a pan on the stove over medium heat and pan fry until golden and crispy. 
Salad: divide the spinach, cucumber, carrot, red onion, herbs, avocado and chickpeas between 3 meal prep containers. Top each with ¼ cup feta. Add the crispy lavash to the salad or keep it on the side until eating.
Dressing: in a jar or measuring glass, mix the tahini, lemon juice and greek yogurt with a pinch of salt until light in color and creamy. Keep the dressing on the side until you eat.

This salad can last in the fridge for up to 4 days with hte dressing on the side. Crispy lavash can be stored in an airtight container at room temp for 5-6 days.

description:
Back to School / Meal Prep Snack Idea: Zesty Gluten Free Chex Mix

This Zesty Gluten-Free Chex Mix is crunchy, savory, and super easy to make in bulk. It’s the kind of snack that actually satisfies you in between meals… without a ton of effort.

I love having a batch of this ready for the afternoon slump or packing it in my bag for on-the-go days. It’s also super customizable based on what you have on hand!

Here’s what you’ll need to make it:

🥣 Ingredients
	•	2 cups gluten-free Chex cereal
	•	1 1/2 cups gluten-free pretzels
	•	1/2 cup raw almonds
	•	3 tbsp unsalted melted butter
	•	1 tsp powdered buttermilk
	•	1/2 tsp dried chives
	•	1/4 tsp dried dill
	•	1/4 tsp salt
	•	1/8 tsp garlic powder

👩‍🍳 To make it:
	1.	Preheat oven to 250ºF. Line a 9x13 baking sheet with parchment.
	2.	Add Chex, pretzels, and almonds to a medium bowl.
	3.	In a small bowl, stir together melted butter, buttermilk, salt, dill, chives, and garlic powder.
	4.	Pour over the dry mix and gently toss to coat.
	5.	Spread onto the baking sheet and bake for 25-30 mins, stirring once at 15 mins.
	6.	Cool completely before dividing into 4 snack containers.

-1/2 chilli sliced (optional)

-Pour over salad and crumble feta in. 
-Mix well, check for any seasoning and enjoy alone or eat long with protein of choice.
-This keeps for 2 days in the fridge, in a tight storage box. (Trust me - it won’t last that long)

description:
🚨 Done is better than perfect. 🖐🏽
Sweet and Sour salmon meal prep recipe👇🏽 

One of the biggest mistakes I see with meal prep is people waiting for the perfect plan, the perfect grocery list, or the perfect Sunday routine. But the truth is that consistency usually comes from simple meals like this one.

A few ingredients, a hot @charbroilgrills, and dinner is handled for the next few days.

This grilled sweet and sour salmon with pineapple rice is one of those meal preps that feels a little more exciting than the usual chicken and rice, but it’s just as easy to make.

Sweet, savory, and balanced with green beans for a simple meal prep that holds up all week.

Do you agree that done is better than perfect when it comes to meal prep?

Let me know below.

⸻

Grilled Sweet & Sour Salmon with Pineapple Rice Meal Prep
Makes 3 servings

Ingredients
3 salmon fillets (5–6 oz each)
2 cups cooked jasmine rice
1 cup pineapple, diced
2 cups green beans
¼ cup sweet and sour sauce
1 tbsp olive oil
Salt and pepper

Optional
Sesame seeds
Green onion

Instructions

Preheat your grill to medium heat (about 375–400°F).

Season the salmon lightly with salt and pepper, then brush the tops with sweet and sour sauce.

Place the salmon skin-side down on the grill and cook for 8–10 minutes until it flakes easily with a fork. Brush on a little extra sauce during the last few minutes so it caramelizes slightly.

While the salmon cooks, add green beans to a grill basket with olive oil. Cook for about 4–5 minutes until tender and slightly blistered. Season with salt and pepper.

Add the cooked jasmine rice to a foil pan or griddle surface on the grill and fold in the diced pineapple. Warm for 3–4 minutes until heated through.

Divide everything into three meal prep containers with pineapple rice, salmon, and green beans.

Store in the refrigerator for up to three days.

IDK about you, but I LOVE a good casserole 🍳🔥
Today I’m making a Huevos Rancheros Breakfast Casserole, and this one is a guaranteed crowd-pleaser no matter what time of day you eat it.

It’s hearty, flavorful, and perfect for meal prep. I used almond flour tortillas to keep it gluten-free and dairy-free cheese so it works for just about everyone. Big win. 👏🏽

Tag me if you try this one!  I’d love to see it!

Recipe below 👇🏽

Ingredients:
• 6 almond flour tortillas
• 8 eggs
• ½ yellow onion, diced
• 2 cloves garlic, minced
• 1 jalapeño, diced
• 1 avocado, sliced
• 1 can pinto beans, drained
• 1 can crushed red tomatoes
• 2 cups shredded cheese (dairy-free if needed)
• Cilantro or parsley for garnish
• 1 tsp salt
• 1 tsp pepper
• 1 tsp cumin
• 1 tsp chili powder

Directions:
1️⃣ Preheat oven to 400°F.
2️⃣ In a skillet, sauté onion, garlic, jalapeño, and seasonings in olive oil. Add crushed tomatoes and bring to a simmer. Remove from heat.
3️⃣ Layer 3 tortillas in the bottom of a skillet or baking dish. Add half the tomato mixture, half the cheese, and the beans.
4️⃣ Add another layer of tortillas, remaining tomato sauce, and top with cheese.
5️⃣ Use a spoon to make small wells, then crack eggs directly on top.
6️⃣ Bake for 30 minutes, or until egg whites are fully cooked.
7️⃣ Remove from oven, let cool slightly, portion into containers, and top with avocado and herbs.

description:
Sheet Pan Seafood Boil (Easy Weeknight Version) 🌽 🦐 🧄 

Love a seafood boil but don’t want to deal with a giant pot? This sheet pan version gives you all the same buttery, lemony Cajun flavors with way less work.

Ingredients:
• 1 lb @melissasproduce baby Dutch yellow potatoes (halved)
• 2 ears corn (cut into thirds)
• 12 oz smoked sausage (sliced)
• 1 lb shrimp (peeled & deveined)
• 4 tbsp butter (melted)
• 1 lemon (sliced)
• 1–1½ tbsp Cajun seasoning

Instructions:

1️⃣ Preheat oven to 400°F.

2️⃣ Toss potatoes with half the butter and Cajun seasoning.
Spread on a sheet pan and roast 15 minutes.

3️⃣ Add sausage and corn to the pan. Roast 10 minutes.

4️⃣ Add shrimp and lemon slices. Drizzle remaining butter and seasoning.
Roast 6–8 minutes until shrimp are cooked through.

5️⃣ Serve straight from the pan and squeeze the roasted lemon over everything.

Meal prep tip:
Line your sheet pan with parchment or foil. The butter and seasoning caramelize a little while roasting and the cleanup is way easier.

🔥 Save this recipe for your next easy dinner and tag someone who loves seafood boils.

title:
How to pick out the perfect watermelon every time. 

There are 5 main tests I put a watermelon through to pick out the best one. Usually it starts by going straight to the bin with the seeded watermel
description:
How to pick out the perfect watermelon every time. 

There are 5 main tests I put a watermelon through to pick out the best one. Usually it starts by going straight to the bin with the seeded watermelons but sometimes the store doesn’t have any so I have to settle for seedless and here are the test I used to judge my watermelons. 

Test 1: The weight test. A good watermelon will be heavy relative to its size. 

Test 2: the knock test. Listen for a deep hollow sound that holds a little bit of reverb, you should almost hear the sound travel through the watermelon and out the backside. 

Test 3: the type test. Seated watermelons are almost always better than seedless, but all that is available is a seedless watermelon, these tests still hold true. 

Test 4: the field spot test. A watermelon with a big, creamy yellow field spot usually means it had time to ripen on the vine sitting in the field. 

Test 5: the webbing test. The brown woody looking spots are called webbing. It’s where bees leave tiny scars on the fruit as they pollinate the flowers. The webbing is a good indicator of sweetness because well pollinated watermelons tend to have higher sugar content. 

You can also look at the vine end of the watermelon and if it is brown instead of green, that can be a good sign that it has been enough time to ripen. 

There’s a full length video where I go into detail of how I pick watermelons as well as how I cut them in order to remove every single seed. And I mean that every single seed not just the black ones. It’s on my YouTube channel. Just search for my name or the meal prep mania and you’ll find it.

Sausage Egg & Cheese Savory Baked Oatmeal. Start meal prepping your breakfasts and you will change your mornings. Can you imagine what a few extra minutes of beauty sleep will do? 

Full Recipe: https
description:
Sausage Egg & Cheese Savory Baked Oatmeal. Start meal prepping your breakfasts and you will change your mornings. Can you imagine what a few extra minutes of beauty sleep will do? 

Full Recipe: https://mealprepmanual.com/sausage-egg-and-cheese-savory-baked-oatmeal/

FOR THE SAUSAGE
1 lb (454 g) ground pork 90/10 any ground meat is okay
1 tbsp (12 g) brown sugar
1 tsp (6 g) salt
1 tsp (3 g) pepper
1 tsp (3 g) cayenne pepper optional for spice
1 tsp (3 g) smoked paprika
1 tsp (3 g) onion powder
1 tsp (3 g) garlic powder
1 tsp (1 g) oregano
1½ tsp (2 g) rubbed sage
1 tbsp (15 g) oil
FOR THE OATMEAL
3 cups (240 g) old fashioned oats
½ cup (60 g) oat flour any flour is fine
2 eggs
2 cups (480 g) 2% milk
1 cup (227 g) cottage cheese
1 cup (112 g) shredded cheddar cheese
1 tsp (4 g) baking powder
½ tsp salt
1 medium (150 g) green pepper
1 small (100 g) onion
1 tbsp (15 g) oil
INSTRUCTIONS
FOR THE BREAKFAST SAUSAGE AND PEPPERS
In a large bowl add the pork with all of the associated seasonings. Mix thoroughly to incorporate into the meat.
In a large skillet over medium high heat, add 1 tbsp of oil and add in the sausage. Brown it on both sides and cook it until no pink color remains. Be careful not to burn the sugars.
Break up the sausage into small pieces as it cooks and set aside until you are ready for it later.
While the sausage is cooking cut your onion and pepper into a small dice. Once the sausage has finished, remove it from the pan and add another 1 tbsp of oil. Add the onions and peppers and cook for a few minutes to develop color. Season lightly with salt.
FOR THE BAKED OATMEAL
Preheat your oven to 375 °F.
In a large bowl, beat 2 eggs, add the milk and cottage cheese and mix together.
Next add in the oats, flour, baking powder, salt, sausage and peppers, and cheddar cheese. Mix to combine.
Spray a 13”x9” pan with oil and add the oat mixture. Spread evenly across the pan.
Bake for 40-45 minutes or until set in the center.
PLATING
This recipe makes 6 servings. Cut the oatmeal into 6 equal pieces.
NUTRITION
Calories: 569kcal | Carbohydrates: 46g | Protein: 36g | Fat: 27g | Fiber: 7.8g

description:
Comment ‘HSR’ and we’ll send you this entire conversation.

@jackieaina went from being paid $300 per month in the Army to one of the loudest voices in beauty on YouTube.

At a time when makeup counters didn’t even display her shade, Jackie took a stand and created content that highlighted the non-inclusive beauty space. 

And one day, the brands started listening. 😳

Today, she is the founder of best selling brand at Sephora @forvrmood and has helped change the beauty industry for black women forever. 

She has not only become friends with some of the biggest tastemakers in beauty but has also established herself as one. 

Here’s everything we cover: 

💅 Why she is called the ‘Queen of Blocking’

💅 Selling out 6 months’ worth of inventory in 4 hours (on her first launch…) 

💅 Why successful people never wear sweatpants outside the house

💅 Why she does NOT want to build a $1B company 

💅 The mentality behind posting for 4 years before her first viral video

None of this came easy but she did two things that many others couldn’t - she stayed consistent and maintained a point of view.

Jackie, we loved talking to you and we can’t wait for everyone to hear your story.

Jackie Aina, are you ready to get Hot Smart Rich?

title:
There’s still too much misinformation about sunscreen online. This has real consequences: it reduces sunscreen use, and harms public health outcomes.
 
That’s why a group of scientists from fields inc
description:
There’s still too much misinformation about sunscreen online. This has real consequences: it reduces sunscreen use, and harms public health outcomes.
 
That’s why a group of scientists from fields including photobiology, dermatology, solar physics, and behavioural science came together to write “A Manifesto for Informed Sun Protection Advice in Relation to Sunscreens”. 

This is an accessible, evidence-based document that clearly outlines what scientists agree on about sunscreen and sun protection, and some common myths.

This is a great example of scientists working to improve public understanding! 

The manifesto is publicly available - you can easily find it by searching the title online. Please read and share!

See also our other content for more detailed info on sunscreen myths 🤓

#sunscreen #SPF #science #misinformation

description:
If a new form of sunscreen seems too good to be true… there’s a good chance it’s because you aren’t applying enough.

At the same time, there ARE lightweight sunscreens that don’t give a white cast and feel almost like moisturiser, with the FULL application amount!

The best sunscreen is the one you’ll apply ENOUGH OF, regularly.

This means around ¼ teaspoon for your face alone, 1 shotglass for your body.

Comment YESPF for a DM with my top sunscreen recs, SPF FAQs and SPF myth directory 🤓

title:
#stitch with @washingtonpost Anytime you hear "fragrances are bad for your health because of phthalates", it's wrong on a pretty basic level…

Phthalates are a class of ingredients with very different
description:
#stitch with @washingtonpost Anytime you hear "fragrances are bad for your health because of phthalates", it's wrong on a pretty basic level…

Phthalates are a class of ingredients with very different properties. It's like how alcohols can go from very toxic (methanol = 1 carbon) to not that bad (ethanol = 2 carbons), to moisturising (fatty alcohols = 10+ carbons) just by adding extra carbon atoms.

The phthalates linked to health effects aren't used in fragrances or other cosmetics - they don't have any function in them. They're used as plasticisers (and the evidence there is still not unequivocal)!

The only phthalate used in fragrances is diethyl phthalate, because it's been repeatedly found to be safe.

I've been working on a fragrance science video - what other fragrance topics would you like me to cover?

#fragrance #mythbusting #phthalates #nontoxicliving

title: #stitch with @doctormyro A lot of chemical sunscreen fear is because of animal/in vitro studies taken out of context, without comparing the amounts in those studies to the amounts we're exposed to fro
description:
#stitch with @doctormyro A lot of chemical sunscreen fear is because of animal/in vitro studies taken out of context, without comparing the amounts in those studies to the amounts we're exposed to from using sunscreens. 
 
Safety limits are set with massive buffers (100-fold margin of safety, from e.g. the no observed adverse effect level).

It's also important to consider the downsides of the alternatives - mineral sunscreens have a lot of drawbacks, very few people end up being able to use them regularly (if you genuinely prefer mineral sunscreens that's fine, just watch out for separation and adequate application!)

The best sunscreen is the one you can use a lot of, regularly - and don't forget to use sunscreen in conjunction with protective clothing, hats, shade and sunglasses when the UV index is set to hit 3 or over 😎

#sunscreen #sunprotection #science
author: labmuffinbeautyscience

Also side note: The problem with fossil fuels is when they're burnt for energy - during combustion, the carbons in t
description:
Another ingredient people think is banned in the EU: petroleum jelly (petrolatum).

Also side note: The problem with fossil fuels is when they're burnt for energy - during combustion, the carbons in them are combined with oxygen in the air to form CO2, a greenhouse gas.

Petroleum jelly itself does not contribute much to anthropogenic climate change (not significantly more or less than alternative moisturising ingredients).

#skincarescience #mythbusting #cleanbeauty
